question: When a company hires regular service from external sources which was previously provided internally is known as ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Outsourcing**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Outsourcing** refers to the practice where a company contracts external organizations or service providers to handle tasks, services, or functions that were previously managed internally by its employees. 
• This process is often adopted to improve efficiency, reduce costs, or focus resources on core business activities. 
• Outsourcing is commonly applied to areas like **IT services, customer support, manufacturing, accounting, human resources, and logistics**. 
• It enables organizations to leverage specialized expertise or technology from external vendors while freeing up internal resources. 
• Outsourcing can be implemented domestically (within the same country) or internationally (often referred to as offshore outsourcing). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Subsidization:** 
• Subsidization refers to financial assistance provided by a government or organization to reduce the cost of goods, services, or production for specific groups or industries. 
• It is often employed to support sectors like agriculture, education, renewable energy, or healthcare. 
• Unlike outsourcing, subsidization does not involve delegating tasks to external entities but focuses on monetary aid. 
• Example: Government subsidies for farmers to purchase fertilizers or seeds at reduced costs. 
• **Cross-Subsidization:** 
• Cross-subsidization occurs when revenue from one product, service, or customer group is used to subsidize another product, service, or customer group. 
• This is a common practice in industries like telecommunications, where profits from urban areas may subsidize services in rural areas. 
• It focuses on balancing costs across different segments rather than outsourcing or external contracting. 
• Example: A mobile service provider charging higher rates for premium services to subsidize basic services for low-income users. 
• **Globalization:** 
• Globalization refers to the integration of economies, cultures, and societies across the globe through trade, investment, technology, and information exchange. 
• While outsourcing is a result of globalization, the two are distinct concepts. Globalization is a broader phenomenon, while outsourcing is a business strategy within this framework. 
• Example: Companies setting up manufacturing units in foreign countries to benefit from lower labor costs. 
• Important Points: 
• Outsourcing is driven by factors like cost reduction, access to specialized skills, scalability, and focus on core competencies. 
• It can take various forms, including **offshore outsourcing** (to other countries) and **domestic outsourcing** (within the same country). 
• Challenges of outsourcing include **loss of control, dependency on external vendors, quality concerns, and potential data security risks**. 
• Examples of outsourcing include customer service call centers, IT support, payroll processing, and manufacturing of products like electronic components. 
• Major countries for offshore outsourcing include **India, China, the Philippines, and Eastern Europe**, known for skilled labor at competitive costs. </ul
